evidence: Egeria, Itin. 25: fit ergō prīmā diē missa in ecclēsiā majōre
terms.comment: The Western name, from the dismissal that ends the service: in Egeria (c. 384) missa is still that dismissal, and so the service itself (fit missa); Lewis & Short cite Ambrose for the Mass. In the Eastern churches the same service is the Divine Liturgy.

evidence: Plaut., Ter., Cic. ND 3.47 (Lewis & Short s.v. dīvīnus)
terms.comment: Classically a sacrifice, an act of worship (rē dīvīnā factā, Plaut.; Lewis & Short); Vives uses it of the Mass (Morgan–Owens).

evidence: M-O s.v. service: mass: hear mass (Tursellinus, 1652)
terms.comment: A sacred rite; the Renaissance said sacrum audīre, to hear Mass (Morgan–Owens).

sources: Lewis & Short: missa · Lewis & Short: res · Lewis & Short: divinus · Lewis & Short: sacrum
